what: Deposit-to-results-tree consistency scan: every cell tag referenced by a RUN_*_cell*.json deposit, resolved against the SCONE results directory.
scope_checked: All 133 distinct cell tags referenced by RUN_*_cell*.json deposits in paper/.
why_this_class: The r280 provenance break was a citing file disagreeing with its source. This is the same class across the paper/-to-results boundary, which a reader confined to paper/ cannot check at all.

DUPLICATE_TWINS.GOOD_NEWS: In ALL FOUR the deposit result_dir points at the COMPLETE copy. No deposited result was computed from a truncated twin, and the >=91-line guard independently selects the same complete copy in three of the four.
DUPLICATE_TWINS.THE_TRAP: R294FAST_s102 is different in kind. BOTH its directories exceed 91 history lines (551 and 601), so the guard cannot discriminate and any tag-based resolver using 'assert len(g) == 1' RAISES on this cell. The 600-generation arm needs the >=601 guard, and even that leaves the bare 551 copy passing a >=91 test.
DUPLICATE_TWINS.RULE: For r294, and for any arm whose duplicate twins both clear the generation guard, cells MUST be resolved through the deposit result_dir field, never through the tag. Tag resolution is safe only where exactly one twin clears the guard, which is a property of the data and not of the resolver.
DUPLICATE_TWINS.ORIGIN: These twins are the SO-26 interruption pattern on disk: a killed cell leaves a short-history directory and the restart writes a ' (1)' copy alongside it. The bare tag sorts FIRST, so a resolver taking the first match gets the truncated run.

what_a_reader_cannot_check: Whether the bare-tag twins were killed runs or aborted starts is not recorded anywhere in paper/; it is inferred from their short histories and from no deposit referencing them.
